name: Blossom Commons
headline: Volker Development is building Blossom Commons, 50 one- and two-bedroom apartments for adults 55+ earning 30% to 70% AMI on city-donated land in Downtown Westminster. It won 2025 Round One federal 9%, state and TOC credits from CHFA and broke ground on 2026-04-14.
why_it_matters: It shows a city land-write-down model: the Westminster Economic Development Authority gave the land for $1, the city added fee rebates, a ground-floor lease and its HOME allocation, and in return got a 60-year affordability term in its redeveloped downtown.

status.label: Under construction (groundbreaking 2026-04-14)
status.detail: Downtown Westminster reports the project broke ground on 2026-04-14, after Boston Capital Finance announced on 2026-03-23 that it had closed a forward permanent loan. The project website says applications are not open yet. No completion date or building permit record was found.

next_step: Watch for the opening of the leasing interest list on the project website and a certificate of occupancy for 9145 Eaton Street.

key_numbers.meaning: 25 one-bedroom and 25 two-bedroom units for households at 30% to 70% AMI; 20 units at or below 50% AMI.
About $16M over the 10-year credit period, plus $650,000 state credit and $65,000 TOC credit.
City-owned downtown parcel valued at $306,500, plus $628,515 in fee waivers and rebates and part of the streetscape costs.
As stated at the April 2026 groundbreaking; a December 2024 city staff report put it at $24 million.

facts.value: Southwest corner of 91st Place and Eaton Street (CHFA); 9145 Eaton Street, Westminster, CO 80031 (project website). About 1.4 acres bounded by 90th Avenue, Eaton Street, 91st Place and Fenton Street, next to the Bowlero bowling alley
N, OA: new construction, older adult

One three-story elevator building with double-loaded interior hallways; post-tension slab, wood frame, flat TPO roof; brick, metal and cementitious siding. One-bedrooms are about 600 sq ft and two-bedrooms about 800 sq ft
Surface parking at 0.8 spaces per unit; the city allowed surface instead of structured parking and eased facade standards
Commercial space to be leased by the City of Westminster for a Community Resource Center
Within a half mile of the US 36 and Sheridan bus rapid transit station (Flatiron Flyer). A $150,000 transportation reserve funds bus passes
LEED Silver target; 2021 IECC; 3 EV charging spaces plus EV-ready and EV-capable spaces
60 years (deed restriction tied to the WEDA land donation)
Called Aster Place in late 2024 and Blossom Crossing in later Westminster planning documents

background.text: The site is part of the 105-acre Downtown Westminster redevelopment on the former Westminster Mall, which the city bought between 2009 and 2011. The city aims for 15 to 20 percent of downtown housing to be affordable.
In December 2024 City Council approved a $1 purchase and sale agreement with Volker for the then-named Aster Place senior project; Councilmember Kristine Ireland cast the lone no vote.
The applicant said the land purchase contract would end on 2026-03-31, which together with the November 2025 council election made an early credit award urgent.
The city moved the building footprint so the site fell inside the DOLA Transit-Oriented Communities buffer.
In October 2025 BizWest reported Volker had received the city's go-ahead for a development agreement for the project, called Blossom Crossing in planning documents.
City due diligence flagged possible abandoned asbestos-containing utility pipes under the site; the application says abatement is in the construction budget.
Services: an on-site resident services navigator paid from the operating budget. The city plans to restart a Via Mobility partnership for senior and disabled riders.
The market study cited by the applicant found 97% occupancy at comparable senior LIHTC properties and projected lease-up of about 15 units per month.

discrepancies.text: The December 2024 city staff report as reported by Colorado Community Media described 24 one-bedroom and 25 two-bedroom units with 8 at 30% AMI, 14 at 50%, 14 at 60% and 14 at 80%, while CHFA's award lists 25 one-bedroom and 25 two-bedroom units with 5 at 30%, 15 at 50%, 14 at 60% and 16 at 70% AMI.
The December 2024 staff report put the project cost at $24 million, while the 2026 groundbreaking post says $26 million.
CHFA describes the land as donated by WEDA, while the city's agreement sells it for $1.
